sections.brief: Hook: the famous problem neuron, superposition, and the thesis. FRAME 0 IS THE THUMBNAIL: bring in `scope` (fade-in/scale-in) and `neuron` (pop) with `at: start-0.5` so the lens and cell are already visible at t=0, plus a small muted caption 'a famous problem neuron' words-in near the top of the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000). cue:cats → a slide-label chip 'cat faces' pops to the right of the lens, with a thin cyan line drawn from `cell.right` to it; cue:cars → a second chip 'car fronts' below it, same treatment. cue:superposition → an `old`-rose label 'superposition' words-in under the chips. cue:knot → a tangled knot (an svg/path scribble stroked `old`, ~240px) draws on over the cell inside the lens, and the cell dims slightly (to opacity ~0.6 via `to`, restored before the end). cue:second → a small dashed card 'second model (SAE)' rises in on the right with a short arrow 'unfold'. Around 'the knot was never there' (just before cue:clean) the knot draw-offs/fades and the old labels and chips clear (sink-out / clear). cue:clean → the title 'neural networks are already clean' (h2, two lines OK) words-in in the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000), with a muted caption 'Nick Cammarata · Goodfire' under it; the cell pulses once in `cell` cyan. Hold briefly, then `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s1: scope and neuron fully visible, unscaled, cell back at full opacity.

The cat/car neuron is a V detector. Lens and cell stay. 'Look at that neuron again, and ask what one thing it sees' → small muted caption 'what one thing?' near top of the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000). On 'cat ears, car grilles, fox snouts' pop three chips stacked in the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000): 'cat ears', 'car grilles', 'fox snouts', each with a tiny drawn V-ish glyph (a chevron path) beside it in `cell`. cue:point → the three chevrons pulse together. cue:vee → a large amber (`fix`) V (stroke-only chevron, ~180px tall) draws on inside the lens to the upper-right of the cell, and an amber label 'V detector' words-in in the workspace; the chips dim. cue:oh → below the cell inside the lens, a muted ring 'O' (stroke-only circle ~110px) scale-ins with a small '−' badge (negative side), and a muted caption 'round things push it down' words-in in the workspace, optionally with two tiny round glyphs (circles) 'golf ball', 'clock' as labels. `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s2 (scope + neuron unchanged).

The textbook 'superposition circuit' was shared pose. Inside the lens, the cell is the car neuron: a small chip 'car' pops beside it at cue:car. cue:dogs → four small neuron circles (r≈34, fill `cellDim`, stroke `cell` thin) pop in a column on the right side of the lens (stagger 0.1), with arrows drawing on from `cell` to each; each gets an `old`-rose label 'dog' in the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000) (list aligned with the circles), and a muted caption 'hidden storage?' words-in. On 'the visualizations kept sliding into dogs' a small muted note 'feature visualization fell into dogs' appears (top of the workspace). cue:through → the four 'dog' labels cross out/fade (sink-out) and amber (`fix`) labels land in their place, in order: 'car', 'car', 'pose', 'pose' (stagger 0.15); cue:pose → the two 'pose' circles pulse and an amber caption 'shared car + dog pose' words-in. `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s3.

InceptionV1's messy last layer vs. a modern network the same size. Use the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000) for two specimen trays stacked vertically (each a card with a 10×2 grid of small square 'neurons', ~44px squares). Top tray, at cue:none: label 'InceptionV1 · last layer' (muted); its squares pop in mostly `cellDim` with only one lit `cell` square (shows 'almost none'); the cell in the lens dims to `cellDim` fill (via `to`, restore before end). cue:same → bottom tray rises in: label 'modern network · same size · 7.06M'; two small chips 'residual connections' and 'layer norm' pop beside its label. cue:nearly → the bottom grid's squares light to `cell` in a quick left-to-right stagger (0.03), and an amber stat '99–100%' (count-up to 99 then the text '99–100%' is fine, or just pop the text) lands next to the tray with caption 'easy to read'. On 'a learning problem, not superposition' an amber caption 'a learning problem' words-in and an `old` 'superposition' label strikes through (a line draws across it). `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s4 (cell back to its base fill).

Recursive generalization: neurons grow like branches. cue:branch → an amber title 'recursive generalization' is NOT shown yet; first a muted caption 'grows like a branch'. Draw a branching tree out of the cell: curved arrows (bend) from `cell.right` reaching into the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000). cue:iy → first node: a small `cell` circle with chip 'iy' at the end of the first branch (upper). Optionally a side twig to a chip 'Miyazaki' (also contains 'iy'). cue:diy → a second branch grows from the 'iy' node to a node 'diy'. cue:diyfull → a third branch grows from 'diy' to an amber node 'do it yourself', with a tiny tag 'no “iy”'. cue:recursive → amber h2 'recursive generalization' words-in at the top of the workspace, and two short contrasting captions below the tree: 'similar things' in `fix` amber vs 'not unrelated ones' with an `old` 'superposition' struck through. `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s5.

Language models, then and now. In the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000): a small header 'language model neurons' (muted). cue:onepoint → row 1: label '2023 · automated study' and a horizontal track (~700px) with a tiny `old` fill wiping to 1.7% of the track, value '~1.7% interpretable' popping at its end. cue:ninety → row 2: label 'now · Qwen3-32B (early audit)' and a stacked bar on the same 0–100% scale: `cell` segment 90% wipes in with label 'one main job ~90%'; cue:seven → an amber `fix` segment ~7% appends with label 'two related jobs ~7%'; cue:few → a `muted` segment 2–4% (draw ~3%) with label 'not yet understood 2–4%'. Segment widths proportional. cue:trillions → a chip 'holds up to trillions of parameters' pops below. The lens cell glows: pulse + brief `to` fill `cell` and back. `clear` at end-0.6. End on key s6. Real numbers only.

Payoff and end card (last section; final picture holds ≥3 s). cue:crossword → inside the lens, a small crossword of square 'neurons' (~56px squares in a plus/cross pattern around and including the cell area, 8–10 squares) appears as `cellDim` outlines, then fills to `cell` one square at a time (stagger ~0.25 s) — each solved square constrains its neighbours; a muted caption 'understanding compounds' words-in in the workspace (right-half region, x ≥ 1000). cue:bitter → an amber caption 'a bitter lesson for interpretability?' words-in in the workspace with a small muted line 'scale ordinary investigation'. On 'It's a working hypothesis' a muted chip 'a working hypothesis' fades in. cue:study → clear the captions (words-out) and the crossword squares fade, leaving the clean lens and cell; then the end card: h2 'neural networks are already clean' words-in in the workspace (as in s1), with the muted credit 'Nick Cammarata · Goodfire · 2026' and the cell pulsing once at cue:end. Land the final picture on the last spoken line and hold it.
